newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler director snaps up shares - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler director snaps up shares - WSJ.

text.p: Chrysler Corp director John Neff bought $1.4 million of the auto maker's stock last month at a time when others on Wall Street were shying away from the shares, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said Neff, a high-profile money manager, bought 50,000 shares on April 15 at prices ranging between $28.63 and $28.88 each.
The purchases came after Chrysler's stock price dropped amid concerns about slowing sales, a rising dollar and higher interest rates, the Journal said.
The purchases were outlined by Disclosure Inc., which processes all insider filings on behalf of the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Neff was out of the country and unavailable to comment.
A Chrysler spokesman said he bought the shares on the first day of the most recent 30-day period during which Chrysler executives and directors are allowed to trade shares.
Neff had owned 33,944 Chrysler shares as of March 31, according to a proxy statement.
